summary:
Nature Signals is a hydrological intelligence platform designed to make complex Earth science data accessible and useful to communities that depend on Amazonian rivers.

Developed by team Manaós Espacial for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the platform combines historical river discharge observations from Brazil's National Water Agency (ANA), probabilistic forecasts from Copernicus GloFAS, and environmental information from NASA POWER.

Users can select a river section and forecast period to explore expected discharge trends, historical patterns, statistical significance, and forecast uncertainty. Instead of presenting complex scientific data without context, Nature Signals translates the results into clear explanations that support informed decisions.

The platform does not claim to measure water depth or guarantee safe navigation. Its purpose is to help communities, researchers, and river transport operators better understand hydrological changes.

Our future vision includes IoT sensors installed on vessels to collect local river observations, connecting satellite-based science, hydrological models, and community knowledge.
details:
Nature Signals — Project Details

1. The Problem

In the Amazon Basin, rivers are essential for transportation, commerce, food distribution, healthcare, education, and the daily lives of local communities.

However, understanding changes in river conditions is challenging because hydrological information is often fragmented, highly technical, and difficult for non-specialists to interpret.

Scientific institutions provide valuable historical observations, environmental measurements, and hydrological forecasts, but transforming these datasets into understandable information remains a significant challenge.

Our team, Manaós Espacial, created Nature Signals to bridge the gap between Earth science data and the people who depend on Amazonian rivers.

2. Our Solution

Nature Signals is an open-source web application designed to detect, analyze, visualize, and communicate river-flow trends in the Amazon Basin.

The platform transforms complex scientific information into accessible insights that support informed decisions.

Users can select a river corridor, forecast issue date, and prediction horizon of up to 30 days.

The application provides:

  • Probabilistic river discharge forecasts.
  • P50 median values and P10–P90 uncertainty intervals.
  • Historical trends and climatological comparisons.
  • Recent hydrological anomalies.
  • Statistical significance indicators.
  • Clear explanations of expected increases, decreases, or stable discharge conditions.
  • Progress indicators, warnings, and partial results during data processing.
  • Explicit uncertainty and navigation-related limitations.

Instead of presenting technical measurements without context, Nature Signals translates scientific evidence into understandable information.

3. Scientific Data and Methodology

Nature Signals integrates three important scientific data sources.

ANA — Brazilian National Water Agency

Historical river discharge observations provide the foundation for climatological analysis, historical comparisons, anomaly detection, and statistical trend evaluation.

The platform uses up to ten years of historical reference data and applies statistical methods including Sen's slope and the Mann–Kendall test.

Copernicus / GloFAS

The Global Flood Awareness System provides probabilistic river discharge forecasts based on ensemble modeling.

Nature Signals analyzes forecasts containing 50 ensemble members and presents the P50 median as the central forecast, alongside the P10–P90 interval to communicate uncertainty.

NASA POWER

NASA environmental datasets provide complementary information about meteorological and environmental conditions, helping contextualize hydrological behavior.

By combining historical observations, probabilistic forecasts, and environmental context, the platform helps users understand what is changing, how it is changing, and whether historical trends are statistically significant.

4. Technical Architecture

The project consists of four main components.

Frontend

The responsive web interface is developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG charts.

It enables users to interact with hydrological forecasts, visualize uncertainty intervals, compare historical trends, and understand statistical results.

The interface also provides progress status, warnings, and partial results, improving transparency when external scientific data services require additional processing time.

Backend

The scientific backend is developed in Python, using:

  • FastAPI
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • xarray
  • httpx
  • Uvicorn

It connects to official scientific data services, retrieves and normalizes hydrological and environmental datasets, performs statistical analysis, calculates historical trends and anomalies, and exposes REST API endpoints to the frontend.

Data and Intelligence Layer

The system combines ANA historical observations, Copernicus/GloFAS probabilistic forecasts, and NASA POWER environmental data.

An AI-assisted intelligence layer provides auxiliary interpretation and confidence signals.

Importantly, artificial intelligence does not replace the statistical calculations or official scientific observations.

The core hydrological analysis remains grounded in historical measurements, established statistical methods, and recognized forecast products.

When the available information is insufficient to support a reliable classification, the platform explicitly communicates uncertainty instead of presenting an unsupported conclusion.

Persistence and Infrastructure

The persistence service uses Node.js, Prisma, and PostgreSQL.

The applications are containerized using Docker and orchestrated with Docker Compose.

Nginx provides reverse proxy routing, HTTPS, and secure access to public services.

This architecture separates scientific processing, user interaction, and data persistence, supporting maintainability and future expansion.

5. Innovation and Creativity

Nature Signals goes beyond traditional hydrological dashboards by combining scientific analysis, probabilistic forecasting, accessible communication, and AI-assisted interpretation.

Its innovation lies in making complex Earth science data understandable without hiding uncertainty.

The platform distinguishes historical trends from future predictions, explains statistical significance, and communicates the limitations of available evidence.

For example, river discharge is not equivalent to water depth, and the platform does not claim that discharge forecasts alone can determine safe navigation conditions.

This approach prioritizes scientific transparency and responsible decision support.

6. Benefits and Social Impact

Nature Signals was designed for people and organizations that depend on river information, including:

  • River-dependent and riverside communities.
  • Boat operators and river transportation services.
  • Local authorities and environmental organizations.
  • Researchers and scientific institutions.

By making hydrological information easier to understand, Nature Signals aims to improve environmental awareness, support operational planning, and strengthen access to scientific knowledge.

Our objective is not to replace local experience, but to complement it with accessible scientific evidence.

7. Future Development — IoT and Connected Rivers

The current minimum viable product (MVP) is fully web-based and does not yet include physical sensors.

Our future roadmap includes installing Internet of Things (IoT) devices on vessels that regularly navigate Amazonian waterways.

These devices could collect georeferenced measurements of water depth, flow conditions, and vessel location in near real time.

By combining scientific forecasts with local observations, Nature Signals could evolve into a collaborative river-monitoring network.

This future capability could help improve the relationship between hydrological forecasts and actual river conditions, supporting more informed decisions for communities and transportation operators.

The approach could eventually be adapted to other river basins around the world.

8. Team and Project Resources

Team: Manaós Espacial

9. Our Vision

We believe scientific knowledge becomes more valuable when people can understand and use it.

Nature Signals connects Earth science, technology, and local knowledge to help communities better understand the rivers that shape their lives.

Nature Signals — Turning scientific data into better-informed decisions for people who depend on rivers.
